Frequently Asked Questions
What is alternative cancer treatment at ITC Immunity Therapy Center?
Alternative cancer treatment at ITC refers to customized modalities—such as specialized immunotherapies, hyperthermia, and biomagnetic therapy—designed to support the immune system and target cancer cells. As a specialized cancer immunotherapy treatment center, ITC designs programs tailored to each patient's needs.
Who may be eligible for alternative cancer treatment at ITC Immunity Therapy Center?
Eligibility depends on cancer type, stage, physical strength, organ function, and medical history. Patients undergo a medical evaluation prior to acceptance.
How much does alternative cancer treatment at ITC Immunity Therapy Center cost?
Treatment costs start at $18,995 for standard multi-week programs. Total costs vary based on protocol duration, specific therapies required, and diagnostic needs.
Can alternative cancer treatment be combined with conventional cancer treatment?
Yes, many patients utilize integrative therapies alongside conventional treatments. Any combination should be coordinated with qualified physicians to evaluate safety and compatibility.
What risks should patients consider before choosing alternative cancer treatment?
Patients should consider potential side effects, detox responses, treatment limitations, and personal health conditions before starting therapy.
How do international patients arrange cancer treatment at ITC Immunity Therapy Center?
International patients submit medical records for review, receive a treatment plan and quote, and coordinate travel with ITC's support team.
What medical information should patients provide before consultation?
Patients should provide recent pathology reports, imaging scans (CT, MRI, PET), blood work, diagnosis summaries, and a history of previous treatments.

Sadie Litosky - HODGKIN LYMPHOMA
Sadie Litosky is a brave young girl from Canada. When Sadie was 19, she found out she was very sick with Hodgkin’s Lymphoma, a kind of cancer.
At first, she had a small bump on her neck, but then she started having trouble breathing and felt pain in her chest.
Sadie’s mom searched all over to find help. That’s when they found ITC.
Sadie was not sure about it at first, but she liked how ITC’s plan was gentle and would not hurt her body too much.
At ITC, Sadie got treatments that did not hurt a lot. After just two weeks, she felt better.
Her chest did not hurt anymore, she could breathe easily, and she had more energy. After three and a half months, her cancer was gone!
Sadie loved the kind nurses and doctors at ITC.
Dr. Bautista talked to her honestly, and everyone made her feel safe. Sadie said, “I was welcomed by everyone here, which was really nice, especially when I was scared.” ITC helped Sadie go from feeling scared to feeling hopeful and happy again.

Karla Leonard is a strong and brave woman from California. She had very bad breast cancer that spread to other parts of her body.
Karla felt scared and sad, but she did nt give up hope. She went to ITC for help in May 2013.
At first, Karla’s son was not sure about ITC, but Karla believed it could help her.
When she got there, she saw how kind and caring everyone was. The treatments were gentle and did not hurt her body too much.
Karla liked how the doctors always told her what was happening and how she was getting better.
After three weeks of treatment at ITC in Mexico, Karla went back home.
She kept doing what the doctors told her, like eating healthy food and taking her medicine.
One day, Karla noticed the lumps on her breast were gone! She felt so happy and proud of herself.
Now, Karla does not need her oxygen tank or wheel chair anymore.
She can breathe and walk on her own. Karla knows there are still hard days, but she feels strong and free again.

Beware, the doctors lie to you at this clinic.  I recently went down for 3 weeks of treatment for breast cancer. Even though I told them I didn't want their chemo treatment, they assured me it would be really helpful, they would only be using 10% and I would not lose my hair. They lied. I lost all of my hair which started 1 week after I returned home. When contacting my doctor he told me that was so unusual and recommended Minoxidal (which actually makes your hair shed worse before it regrows).  This happened to 2 other women I kept in contact with. So it wasn't that unusual. When I followed up to find out what they gave me, it was the MOST toxic of all the chemotherapy treatments and they gave me a 50% dose, not 10%. It makes me question everything they are administering here.  It has been extremely stressful which is opposite from what I need healing cancer. I am guessing they push chemo so much because they want results. I later found out the type of cancer I have, isn't responsive to chemotherapy. I would have hoped a clinic like this would have tests to check this. The total disrespect for me to make an informed decision makes me motivated to share my story to help protect others. I regret going here. Spend your money with doctors who are honest.
I will say that the nurses were spectacular. They deserve a 10 star rating. But the doctors deserve a -10 for taking advantage of their patients at their most vulnerable.

FAQs: Alternative Adenocarcinoma Cancer Treatment in Tijuana Mexico
1. What exactly makes ITC's approach "alternative" for adenocarcinoma?
Unlike standard protocols that focus solely on killing cells through toxicity, ITC uses Alternative Adenocarcinoma Cancer Treatment in Tijuana Mexico to strengthen the body's natural defenses. We combine non-toxic therapies with immunotherapy to target glandular cancer cells while maintaining the health of the patient's overall system.
2. Can ITC treat adenocarcinoma that has metastasized?
Yes, we often treat patients with advanced-stage adenocarcinoma. Our protocols focus on systemic immune stimulation, which can be effective in identifying and fighting cancer cells that have spread to other parts of the body.
3. Is the Out-Patient program safe for someone with low energy?
The Out-Patient program is best for those who can move independently. However, if a patient has very low energy or requires constant monitoring due to the severity of their adenocarcinoma, the In-Patient program is highly recommended for 24/7 care.
4. Are the tumor markers checked specifically for glandular cancers?
Absolutely. As part of our weekly lab work, we monitor specific tumor markers relevant to adenocarcinoma, such as CEA or organ-specific markers like PSA or CA 15-3, to measure the real-time effectiveness of the therapy.
5. Why is the treatment period three weeks?
Three weeks is generally the minimum time needed to jumpstart the immune system and begin the detoxification process. It allows the medical team to observe how the adenocarcinoma responds to the initial phase of therapy and adjust the protocol accordingly.
6. Will the ITC doctors work with my oncologist back home?
Yes, we encourage a collaborative approach. Many patients use our Alternative Adenocarcinoma Cancer Treatment in Tijuana Mexico as a complementary therapy alongside their existing medical plans, and we can share results for follow-up care.
7. What kind of nutritional support is provided?
We provide organic, health-optimized meals designed to eliminate toxins and provide the body with the nutrients it needs to recover. This is a core component of our holistic approach to fighting glandular cancer.
8. Is the staff at the clinic bilingual?
Yes, our team is fully bilingual in English and Spanish. This ensures that international patients can communicate clearly with their doctors and nurses regarding every aspect of their adenocarcinoma treatment.

FAQs: Alternative Adrenal Cancer Treatment in Tijuana Mexico
1. Why is Tijuana a hub for alternative adrenal cancer treatments?
Mexico's regulatory environment allows for the use of advanced integrative and alternative therapies that are often caught in long approval processes elsewhere. This allows clinics like ITC to offer the latest innovations in immunotherapy and non-toxic protocols that specifically target endocrine-based malignancies.
2. Can I combine ITC treatments with my current hormone therapy?
Yes, many patients utilize ITC’s protocols as a complementary approach to strengthen their immune system while undergoing conventional hormone management or care elsewhere. Our doctors coordinate closely to ensure therapies do not conflict.
3. How do I know if I am a candidate for the Out-Patient or In-Patient program?
Generally, if you are mobile and have a companion to help with daily logistics, Out-Patient is ideal. In-Patient is reserved for those needing constant nursing care, 24/7 medical monitoring, or those dealing with extreme fatigue from adrenal dysfunction.
4. Are the doctors at ITC board-certified?
Yes, the medical team consists of licensed physicians and specialists with extensive training in both traditional and integrative oncology, ensuring high standards of safety and professional care for every patient.
5. Is English spoken at the clinic?
Absolutely. ITC is designed for international patients, and the entire staff, from doctors to patient coordinators, is fluent in English, ensuring clear communication regarding your treatment plan and progress.
6. What specific tumor markers are monitored for adrenal cancer?
Our weekly lab panels track specific substances and hormones found in the blood that indicate the presence and activity level of adrenal cancer, helping our medical team adjust your protocol based on real-time physiological data.
7. Is Intratumoral Immunotherapy recommended for adrenal tumors?
Intratumoral Immunotherapy is an optional procedure ($6,200 - $7,200) that may be suggested for accessible tumors. The ITC medical board will evaluate your specific scans and case to determine if you are a candidate for this localized treatment.
8. Can I bring my own adrenal support supplements to the clinic?
All supplements and medications will be reviewed by the ITC doctors upon admission to ensure they align with your personalized treatment plan and do not interfere with the active alternative protocols.

Beware, the doctors lie to you at this clinic.  I recently went down for 3 weeks of treatment for breast cancer. Even though I told them I didn't want their chemo treatment, they assured me it would be really helpful, they would only be using 10% and I would not lose my hair. They lied. I lost all of my hair which started 1 week after I returned home. When contacting my doctor he told me that was so unusual and recommended Minoxidal (which actually makes your hair shed worse before it regrows).  This happened to 2 other women I kept in contact with. So it wasn't that unusual. When I followed up to find out what they gave me, it was the MOST toxic of all the chemotherapy treatments and they gave me a 50% dose, not 10%. It makes me question everything they are administering here.  It has been extremely stressful which is opposite from what I need healing cancer. I am guessing they push chemo so much because they want results. I later found out the type of cancer I have, isn't responsive to chemotherapy. I would have hoped a clinic like this would have tests to check this. The total disrespect for me to make an informed decision makes me motivated to share my story to help protect others. I regret going here. Spend your money with doctors who are honest.
I will say that the nurses were spectacular. They deserve a 10 star rating. But the doctors deserve a -10 for taking advantage of their patients at their most vulnerable.

How much does alternative medicine cost abroad compared to domestic prices?
Patients can save 40% to 70% on alternative medicine abroad. Exact prices vary by country and therapy type. Traveling for care remains highly cost-effective.
What types of alternative medicine treatments are available abroad?
Popular treatments include acupuncture, Ayurveda, naturopathy, and stem cell therapy. International wellness centers offer diverse holistic healing options.
Does health insurance cover the cost of alternative medicine abroad?
Most domestic health insurance plans do not cover international alternative therapies. Patients usually pay out-of-pocket or use specialized medical travel plans.
Why is holistic and alternative medicine cheaper abroad?
Lower administrative expenses and reduced living costs make holistic care cheaper. The quality of care remains high despite the significantly lower price tag.
Are alternative medicine practitioners abroad certified and safe?
Yes, many international practitioners hold global certifications. Always verify their credentials and ensure the facility follows strict safety standards.
What hidden costs should I expect when traveling abroad for alternative therapies?
Factor in flights, accommodation, visas, and local transport. Some programs charge extra for post-treatment wellness supplements or extended consultations.
Can I combine a vacation with alternative medicine treatments abroad?
Yes, medical tourism often blends holistic healing with leisure travel. Many wellness retreats are located in popular tourist destinations for optimal recovery.
How do I find affordable alternative medicine packages abroad in 2026?
Compare comprehensive wellness packages that bundle therapies, meals, and lodging. Researching multiple international destinations helps secure the best rates.
